evidence.decision: Reread the complete procedure and Privacy, CareKit, HealthKit and ResearchKit source guides. Feature-purpose minimization, contextual timing and precise permission copy remain the core privacy decisions. The added health branch correctly separates care-plan/task semantics, health-data authorization/sharing, and study participation/informed consent instead of treating a generic permission sequence as the whole domain solution.
evidence.artifact: The procedure still requires a data-purpose/access matrix and corrected permission sequence/copy or implementation in the existing stack. When a health brief contains domain decisions, its conditional owner procedure supplies the corresponding care-task mapping, health-data contract or study onboarding/task/profile sequence; these are usable work products rather than an SDK recommendation.
evidence.transformation: The bird-journal example still concretely removes unrelated launch access and offers supported one-time location at the attachment action. Read the linked health procedures as well: their worked transformations resolve care steps/schedules, purpose-specific health access and eligibility/consent before research permissions. The new paragraph composes those existing operational decisions without replacing the privacy transformation with a topical summary.
evidence.verification: Privacy continues to fail pre-consent collection, misleading purpose copy and optional-access gates, while separating inspected flow from actual system prompts and security/legal certification. The health owners retain checks for accurate task completion, changing authorization and accessible study withdrawal, with clinical efficacy, measurement validity and ethical/legal approval explicitly unverified by static UI work.
evidence.applicability: The source-specific location-button, Mac distribution/user-switching and visionOS private-gaze/Full Space distinctions remain intact. Read the health owner applicability: CareKit and ResearchKit UI guidance is scoped to iOS/iPadOS, with CareKit Watch notifications separately qualified; HealthKit adds watchOS and excludes Mac/TV/visionOS. Consulting experience guidance in an existing stack neither proves SDK availability on another platform nor requires adopting that SDK.
evidence.handoffs: Verified all three new installed-relative links resolve to their current approved procedures. CareKit is conditional on care plans, scheduled treatment actions or symptom/event logging; HealthKit on health-data access/sharing; ResearchKit on actual study participation/research consent. They are not three mandatory reads for every sensitive-data task. Existing Sign in with Apple and AR handoffs remain tied to their actual authentication or sensing branches.
evidence.distinctiveness: The procedure preserves a concrete permission/data-purpose contract and adds a bounded health-domain ownership decision. Care task structure and research consent cannot be inferred from general privacy wording alone, and the framework-agnostic qualification preserves product architecture while allowing those source-specific decisions to be completed.
